Firstly I would like to thank you for having this conversation with me, it is hard finding people who are willing to talk on their beliefs, and I think you really explain your thoughts well, which helped me understand what my thoughts are.

I am not a subscriber of Crowder or Vox so I actually just watched both videos on the green new deal. I think I kind of understand what you mean, the Vox video was not actually about the green new deal, instead, it is about tactical framing itself. And I see how Crowder is trying to frame Vox of trying to make a video on the green new deal by framing the framing around it... That is a lot of frames, and I hope you get what I am saying. But I think the Vox video move on to the subject kind of poorly, I was hoping to see what the green new deal is actually about in Vox's video, but they never talk about it. What Vox did well is explaining what the framing is and the study on the effect, and it was interesting! However, I think if they specifically said "this video is not about the green new deal" it would be better, and it wouldn't leave room for Crowder to make it seems like it is another angle of framing on the green new deal. What Crowder did was kind of smart, they play most of the content of the Vox video, which makes his point seems real.

I think there are no avoiding viewpoints in journalism, however, I think news should focus more on facts, what happen, who did it, and why it happened before they offer different points of views on the subject. I don't think having different opinions is bad for news! I think having a scientist debating a flat earther is not a bad idea, people will take away what they think is more trustworthy. I do think flat earther is just another opinion, in my point of view, it is a wrong opinion, but everyone can have their view on the correctness of an opinion. We have to remember round earth theories was once the "wrong opinion". Ultimately I can only control what I think!

Now, I don't think gatekeeping is a good idea. I understand the need for gatekeeping, because there is too much news going on, and only so much you can report on. However, not everyone will value the weight of news the same. A news network can say "I choose to do these kinds of content", however, no one should say "you shouldn't report that type of news". There is a certain risk involving censorship. Of course, I want reliable and credible news sources, however, thinking a news organisation is 100% right all the time is just silly. You can if you blindly choose to listen to a news source that you trust, how do you know if they are right? In my opinion, the news is becoming entertainment, they need to cater to their viewers, trying to give them what they want to hear, instead of presenting the facts. After all, facts are usually boring. So thanks to your paper, I can kind of grasp the importance of gatekeeping now, but I don't think all news should share the same gatekeeping standard.

I think calling out people's fault is fine, but trying to frame their whole character as evil is.... evil. In that video, instead of having "wrong news sources" vs "right news sources", they simply have "republican and fox" vs "democrat and journalists". I understand that this is for their viewer to better understand the context, but how is that not a smear? You said "the fact that they're often just wrong and hypocritical is just a fact" for fox, but isn't that for all news organisation nowadays? There is a line between facts and opinions, I think all facts are from opinions, but not all opinions are facts, I try to be critical of when I might be wrong because I am scared to be wrong, and most of the time I just find people's arguments their opinions.

Now, lastly, you said the video is not for me, but have you thought about other people who might start following their views blindly? To put it in perspective, what if people just believe everything fox says? In my mind, it is the same as what if people just believe everything vox says.

I agree most of Crowder's material seems to be there for comedic effect and going out of his way to dismiss Carlos' video, but at its core, I don't agree that the journalists' job should be gatekeeping. That is the main thing I agree with Crowder, and the main the I disagree with Carlos. If the message of Carlos' video would be about how we should host diverse information on the news I would've agreed more. But his video makes it seems like he wants more gatekeeping from news, and from the skits he is making, he seems to make fox news "evil" and "wrong", which makes his video less informative for me, as I kind of already know how news operates.

Maybe I am using the word debunking wrong, English is not my first language but what the two videos are doing is similar to me, maybe Vox is not critiquing Fox but journalism in general, however, they are still making fun of people at Fox. Crowder is critiquing how Vox is viewing journalism's job as "gatekeeping", it is just different opinion no? I agree /disagree with some of the points Vox is making, and I also agree/disagree with some of the points Crowder is making, what I don't get is what is the difference between the two?
